clue.text: Mock one Detective Inspector caught breaking regulation

indicators.note: breaking means the regulation word is split open with other letters set into the gap

parts.note: a regulation is a rule
one is the Roman numeral I
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A police officer is mocked after being caught breaking the rules.
explanation.definitionFit: To mock someone is to hold them up to scorn and derision, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Cycled round hot southern island

indicators.note: round means the cycling word goes around the letter for hot

parts.note: to rode is to have ridden, as on a bicycle
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A cyclist toured a hot island in the south.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhodes is a Greek island in the Aegean Sea, so it is an example of an island.

clue.text: Live with wife in small wooded hollow

indicators.note: in puts the letter for wife inside the hollow

parts.note: a dell is a small wooded valley

explanation.surface: A couple make their home in a wooded valley.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwell is to reside or live somewhere, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Sheepdog right for a miner?

parts.note: a collie is a breed of sheepdog

explanation.surface: Is this sheepdog suited to working down a mine?
explanation.definitionFit: A collier is a coal miner, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Sheridan character from close to Cwmbran in Wales —- elderly eccentric

indicators.note: eccentric means the letters are arranged oddly to form a new name
close to picks the final letter of the town name

explanation.surface: An eccentric old character from near a Welsh town appears in a play.
explanation.walkthrough: Lady Sneerwell is the scandal-monger in Sheridan's 'The School for Scandal'. Rearrange N (end of Cwmbran) with WALES and ELDERLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Lady Sneerwell is a character in Sheridan's comedy The School for Scandal, so she is a Sheridan character.

clue.text: Say yes to trust and agree to buy

definitions.meaning: to agree to an offer or proposal
to believe something is true without question
to take an offered item at the stated price

explanation.definitionFit: Each phrase is a sense of the verb: consenting, believing, and taking an offer on goods.

clue.text: Almost heaven, following tea, this French wine

indicators.note: following places the tea word first, with the next piece after it

parts.note: cha is a slang word for tea

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the heaven word is dropped

parts.note: bliss is heaven, perfect happiness

explanation.surface: After tea, this French wine is almost heavenly.
explanation.definitionFit: Chablis is a dry white wine from the Burgundy region of France, an example of French wine.

clue.text: Watch bat in wonder?

parts.note: to eye something is to watch it
an opener is an opening batsman in cricket, a bat

explanation.surface: Spectators stare in wonder at a batsman.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an OPENER is a batsman who starts the innings; a bat can mean a batsman.
explanation.definitionFit: An eye-opener is a surprising revelation, something that causes amazement or astonishment.

clue.text: Attempt to fix a match, all but a farce

indicators.note: to fix means the attempt word is fastened around the other pieces

parts.note: a try is an attempt

indicators.note: all but means the match word loses its last letter

parts.note: a vesta is a kind of match

explanation.surface: An attempt to rig a match turns into a farce.
explanation.walkthrough: A VESTA is an old name for a short wax match.
explanation.definitionFit: A travesty is an absurd or grotesque parody of something, so it is a farce.

clue.text: Again left a site carrying too much

parts.note: over, as in 'do it over', means again
Aden, the Yemeni port, is a place or site

explanation.surface: Someone revisits a place they left, overloaded with baggage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a site' is just a place name here: ADEN, the port in Yemen.
explanation.definitionFit: Overladen means burdened beyond capacity, a direct synonym of carrying an excessive load.

clue.text: Book bridge partners

definitions.meaning: in bridge the players sitting at those compass points play as a pair

explanation.definitionFit: It names Gaskell's industrial novel, and also the two seats that form one partnership at the bridge table.

clue.text: Bowl in field around noon

indicators.note: around tells us the word for field wraps round the letter for noon

parts.note: a field or sphere of activity is an area

explanation.surface: A bowler in a cricket field at midday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bowl' looks like a verb in a cricket scene; it is a noun, a stadium.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowl is an amphitheatre-shaped stadium, which is a kind of arena.

clue.text: Cakes —- girl's got her sixth in her mouth!

indicators.note: the mouth is the front, so the named letter is moved to the start of the girl's name

parts.note: Claire's, a girl's name with possessive s
the sixth letter of Claire is E

explanation.surface: A girl stuffs a sixth cake into her mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: Take CLAIRE'S and move its sixth letter, E, to the front (her mouth).
explanation.definitionFit: Eclairs are long cream-filled choux pastries, a type of cake.

clue.text: Runs slip away causing setback to recovery

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
time is said to elapse, or slip away

explanation.surface: A cricket team losing runs suffers a setback.
explanation.definitionFit: A relapse is a falling back into illness after an apparent improvement, a direct description.

clue.text: Bay and hazel, maybe, on either side of box tree

indicators.note: on either side of puts the first two words around the third, one in front and one behind

parts.note: a bay is a reddish-brown horse
the hazel is an example of a nut
a chest is a box

explanation.surface: Bay and hazel planted around a box hedge make a little woodland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bay' and 'hazel' look like trees; they are a horse and a nut either side of CHEST.
explanation.definitionFit: The horse chestnut is a large deciduous tree bearing conkers, so it is an example of a tree.

clue.text: On air, this rambling chronicler

indicators.note: rambling means the letters wander into a new order

explanation.surface: A rambling historian speaks on the radio.
explanation.definitionFit: A historian records and writes about past events, so is a chronicler.

clue.text: Widest and finest highway in the interior

indicators.note: in the interior means the highway word is placed inside the finest word

parts.note: the best is the finest
a road is a highway

explanation.surface: The finest and widest road runs through the heart of the country.
explanation.definitionFit: Broadest is the superlative of broad, which means wide, so it matches widest.

clue.text: Rail fare may be put away here

definitions.text: Rail fare may be put away here

parts.words: Rail fare may be put away here
parts.note: rail fare reads as a train ticket price but means food eaten on a train, and put away means eaten

explanation.definitionFit: On a train the dining carriage is where travellers eat their meals, the food served on the railway.

clue.text: Style of interior design having red coat applied

indicators.note: applied suggests the letters are put to work again, rearranged into a new form

explanation.surface: A decorating style involving a coat of red paint.
explanation.definitionFit: Art deco is a decorative style of the 1920s and 1930s used in interiors and architecture.

clue.text: Girl eating a chewy sweet

indicators.note: eating means the girl's name surrounds the other letter

parts.note: Carmel is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl munches a toffee.
explanation.definitionFit: A caramel is a chewy toffee-like confection, a type of sweet.

clue.text: Stale pork pie, perhaps, past its sell-by date?

parts.note: something past its sell-by date is old
a pork pie is a style of hat with a flat crown

explanation.surface: A pork pie that has gone past its date is stale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pork pie' looks like food but is a flat-crowned hat style.
explanation.definitionFit: Old hat means old-fashioned and tired, so stale in the sense of unoriginal.

clue.text: Advocate having job holding beer? Just the opposite!

indicators.note: holding means one word is placed inside another
just the opposite reverses the roles, so the beer holds the job instead

parts.note: ale is beer
a post is a job

explanation.surface: A campaigner whose job involves holding a pint of beer.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, POST holds ALE; 'Just the opposite!' swaps that, so ALE holds POST.
explanation.definitionFit: An apostle is a vigorous supporter or advocate of a cause, a noun synonym.

clue.text: Dreamlike, a 50 after county comes up short

indicators.note: after puts the county first, before the other pieces
comes up short means the county name loses its final letter

parts.note: Surrey is an English county south of London
L is the Roman numeral for 50

explanation.surface: A batsman makes a fifty after his county team has been bowled out cheaply.
explanation.walkthrough: SURREY is a county south of London; cut short it gives SURRE.
explanation.definitionFit: Surreal means having the bizarre, irrational quality of a dream, a synonym.

clue.text: Provide witty remark after end of lecture

indicators.note: after says the remark comes behind the letter from lecture
end of picks the last letter of the next word

parts.note: a quip is a witty remark

explanation.surface: A lecturer makes a joke at the end of the talk.
explanation.definitionFit: To equip is to furnish or supply with what is needed, so to provide.

clue.text: Best stretch of thoroughfare, lit extensively

indicators.note: stretch of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Part of a main road is brightly lit along its length.
explanation.definitionFit: The elite are the best of a group, a noun synonym for the pick or cream.

clue.text: Vulgar 10, a tactless talker

parts.note: loud, of clothes or manners, means vulgar or garish
the answer to 10 is cockney rhyming slang for mouth

explanation.surface: A coarse person from the regions who speaks without tact.
explanation.walkthrough: 10 Down is a phrase that is cockney rhyming slang, where a rhyming phrase stands for a word: it means mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: A loudmouth is someone who talks loudly and indiscreetly, a person who speaks without tact.

clue.text: Fibrous tissue beginning to decay in joint

indicators.note: in puts the first letter of decay inside the woodworking joint

parts.note: a tenon is the projecting part of a mortise-and-tenon joint

indicators.note: beginning to picks out just the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Tissue at a joint starting to decay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joint' suggests anatomy, but it is carpentry: a TENON.
explanation.definitionFit: A tendon is a tough cord of fibrous tissue joining muscle to bone, so the description fits.

clue.text: Man, Italian, crossing middle of well-kept quarry

indicators.note: crossing means the man word straddles the middle letters, which go inside it

parts.note: a chap is a man

indicators.note: middle of picks the central letters of the word that follows

parts.note: It is short for Italian, as in It vermouth

explanation.surface: An Italian man walks through a neatly tended quarry.
explanation.definitionFit: A chalk pit is a quarry from which chalk is dug, so it is a specific kind of quarry.
